Notes from the river trail

The trail follows the river for nine miles, and the first stretch is flat, shaded and quiet in the early morning.

Past the old mill the path climbs steeply through birch woods before it drops again toward the water at the second bridge.

I counted forty­two herons over the season, most of them standing perfectly still in the shallows below the weir.

Bring water: there is no fountain between the trailhead and the far car park, and the café there closes at four.
